title: Ratio-Based DI
tagline: Year 2 — Tables where the data is given as ratios of totals

introduction.overview: In a ratio-based DI set the table gives a total and one or more ratios that split it, such as the ratio of males to females or of literate to illiterate persons. To work with it, convert each ratio into actual numbers: if the total is 600 thousand and the ratio is 7 : 5, one part is 50 thousand, so there are 350 thousand males and 250 thousand females. After that, every question is arithmetic on numbers.
introduction.placementRelevance: Ratio-based DI sets are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds and combine ratio skills with table reading.
introduction.realWorldContext: Demographic reports, gender ratios in companies and quality-control splits are presented as ratios.

learningObjectives: Convert a ratio and a total into actual numbers
Handle two ratios on the same total
Compute ratios of derived numbers across rows
Compute totals and percentages from ratios

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: To split T in the ratio a : b, one part = T ÷ (a + b); the shares are a × part and b × part.

coreDefinitions: Ratio a : b: the two quantities are in proportion a to b.
Part value: total divided by the sum of the ratio terms.
Derived number: a count obtained from a total and a ratio.
Two ratios on one total: each ratio splits the same total in a different way.
Simplified ratio: both terms divided by their HCF.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A ratio is a recipe for splitting a total. Add the terms to get the number of parts, divide the total by that to get one part, and then multiply. Different ratios on the same row split the same total in different ways, so each must be converted separately.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Make a table of derived numbers: males, females, literate, illiterate for each city. Do it once and use it for every question.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Splitting a total
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: First share = T × a/(a + b);  second = T × b/(a + b)

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Two ratios
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Split the same total twice, independently

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Percentage from a ratio
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Convert the ratio to a share.

mainNarrative: Start with one row. City A has a population of 600 (thousand) with males to females 7 : 5. The ratio has 12 parts, so one part is 50 thousand: males 350, females 250. The literate to illiterate ratio is 3 : 2 with 5 parts, so one part is 120: literate 360, illiterate 240.
Do the same for every row to make a table of numbers. For C: males 320, females 400, literate 420, illiterate 300. For D: males 270, females 270, literate 240, illiterate 300.

Then answer the questions from the numbers. The city with the least illiterate population is B (480 × 1/6 = 80 thousand). The total number of females in all five cities is 250 + 180 + 400 + 270 + 180 = 1280 thousand.
For ratio questions across rows, simplify the derived numbers: literate in A to literate in B is 360 : 400 = 9 : 10.
Check that the derived numbers add up. Males plus females should equal the city total, and literate plus illiterate should equal the same total.

deepDiveAspects.title: Two ratios do not combine
deepDiveAspects.content: You cannot find the number of literate males from the two given ratios alone, because they split the total in different ways. Questions are designed so that you do not need it.

deepDiveAspects.title: Whole-number check
deepDiveAspects.content: In a well-posed table, derived numbers are usually whole. A fraction signals a misread ratio.

problemVariations.exampleSnippet: Literate in C as a percentage

solvedExamples.title: Split by a ratio
solvedExamples.question: City A has a population of 600 thousand with males to females in the ratio 7 : 5. How many males and females are there?
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: One part = total ÷ sum of terms.

solvedExamples.title: Two ratios
solvedExamples.question: In city B (480 thousand), literate to illiterate is 5 : 1. How many illiterate persons are there?

solvedExamples.title: Ratio of derived numbers
solvedExamples.question: What is the ratio of the number of literate persons in A to that in B?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Divide the total by the sum of the ratio terms to get one part, then multiply. Make a table of numbers once.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Males + females must equal the total; use it to reject options.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: The part value method is the whole technique.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I simplify a ratio of derived numbers?
